blocks.text: Sugar is formed by the reduction of CO₂ by using ATP and NADPH. In this way, CO₂ acts as the source of carbon for making sugars. Carbon dioxide enters the leaves through stomata and gets dissolved in water absorbed by the cell walls of mesophyll cells. Stomata are found in large numbers in leaves. The entry of CO₂ into the leaves is dependent upon the opening of stomata.

About 10% of total photosynthesis is carried out by terrestrial plants, the rest occurs in oceans, lakes and ponds. Aquatic photosynthetic organisms use dissolved CO₂, bicarbonates and soluble carbonates as carbon source. Land photosynthetic organisms use atmospheric CO₂ as carbon source.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Land plants do far more than 10%. Satellite measurements show that land and water each carry out roughly half of the total photosynthesis on Earth: about half by land plants and the other half in oceans, lakes and ponds, mostly by phytoplankton.
Niel’s hypothesis was based on the investigations on photosynthetic bacteria that make carbohydrate from carbon dioxide, but do not release oxygen.
